name: Falcone–Borsellino Airport
before:
Palermo's airport, at Cinisi about 35 km west north west of the city, and second busiest in Sicily after Catania with 9,220,905 passengers in 2025.

The train is the easy way in and often overlooked. Punta Raisi station sits at the airport and is the north western end of the Palermo metropolitan railway, running to Palermo Centrale roughly every 30 minutes from early morning until around ten at night. Buses also run to Palermo, Catania, Messina and across Sicily.

The name carries weight locally. The airport is named after Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino, the two leading anti-mafia judges murdered by the mafia. It was previously called Punta Raisi, after the cape it sits on, and that older name is still in wide use.

It opened in 1960 to replace Boccadifalco, whose short runway and mountainous surroundings made jet operations unsafe.
after:
Palermo's airport, about 35 km west north west of the city. It is the second busiest in Sicily after Catania, with 9,220,905 passengers in 2025.

The train is the easy way in and often overlooked: there is a railway station at the airport, with trains into Palermo.

Its official name is Falcone Borsellino, but the older name, Punta Raisi, is still in use.
